cohort: The study included women diagnosed with gestational diabetes (GDM) who visited a university hospital diabetes clinic, comparing those treated during March-December 2020 (n=417) with those treated during the same period in 2019 (n=430).
finding: Despite earlier GDM diagnosis and higher fasting glucose concentrations during the COVID-19 epidemic, the period did not result in worse glucose control during pregnancy or worse maternal and perinatal outcomes in Slovenia compared to the pre-epidemic year.
mod_finding: No significant difference in caesarean section rates was found between the COVID-19 epidemic period and the preceding year.
gest_age: GDM was diagnosed at a median of 23.9 gestational weeks during the COVID-19 epidemic versus 25.1 gestational weeks in the preceding year.
